Calculate the equal-weight CA radius of gyration of each supplied protein. Which has the larger spatial spread, and what is Rg(1UBQ)/Rg(1CRN)? Does that ranking alone establish which protein is less stably folded?

Coordinates are in angstrom (1 nm = 10 angstrom). XYZ atom rows are one-based after the two header lines. Use the supplied coordinate snapshots without optimization, crystallographic symmetry expansion or periodic wrapping. These are explicitly selected-site models, not complete all-atom or solution-ensemble models. S0006 contains all 76 C-alpha carbon sites of 1UBQ chain A: row i is residue A:i (i=1..76). S0007 contains all 46 C-alpha sites of 1CRN chain A: row i is residue A:i (i=1..46). Each site has equal weight. Do not use mass weights or add waters/side chains. For each structure independently, rbar=(1/N)sum_i r_i and Rg=sqrt((1/N)sum_i||r_i-rbar||^2). Report Rg in nm to three decimals; the ratio is dimensionless. These structures have different sequences and site counts.
